text:
alex: ran a perf sweep on fp8 kernels + new batching heuristics, results look funky :confused:
alex: p95 increased from ~62ms -> ~92ms on short-chat workload after enabling FP8 default kernel
alex: throughput dropped ~18% at 4k concurrent requests
maria: can you paste the exact run command and model config?
alex: `run_prof --model redwood-small-v2 --quant fp8 --batcher dynamic_v2 --kv-warmup=off --concurrency=4000`
jamal: did you enable kv prefetch/warmup? fp8 tends to be sensitive to kv cache occupancy on some kernels
alex: kv-warmup was off for the baseline, same for fp8 run. I suspected warmup but numbers point to kernel selection behaving badly when sequence len < 64
sasha: we saw similar in the lab: FP8 kernel has lower per-token compute but higher kernel launch overhead for tiny seqs + more cache thrash. batching heuristics can hide that if you increase aggregation window
kevin: what about calibration dataset? fp8 accuracy may be forcing fallback paths that slow execution if calibration outliers are present
alex: calibration used our default sample: 5k examples random from logs (avg len 42, long tail). no clip/outlier removal
maria: that could explain it. FP8 per-channel calibration is more fragile to extreme weight activations if data includes long system prompts
jamal: propose: (1) re-run with kv-warmup=partial, (2) try per-tensor calibration vs per-channel, (3) 95/99.9 percentile clipping on activations, (4) tweak batcher aggregation to 10ms window
sasha: agree. also try toggling kernel preference: prefer int8 path for seq<64, fp8 for seq>=64. kernel selector should consider seq distribution, not just model size
alex: quick repro logs attached below:
```
# short run summary
model: redwood-small-v2
quant: fp8
seq_mean: 42
seq_p95: 210
p95_latency_ms: 92 -> baseline 62
throughput_rps: 820 -> baseline 1000
kernel_selected: fp8_fast_kv (for ~70% requests)
kv_cache_misses: increased 3.1x
```
kevin: interesting kv miss spike. maybe ptr-swizzling in the fp8 routine prevents reuse of cached kv buffers -> more allocations
maria: allocation churn + small batches => GC / cudaMalloc latency
jamal: for calibration dataset selection I want a short checklist we can run automatically:
- stratify by sequence length buckets [<=32,33-64,65-128,>128]
- ensure domain mix: system prompts, chit-chat, instructions, code
- drop top 0.1% activation outliers or winsorize at 99.9th pct
- verify per-channel quant stats vs per-tensor; pick per-channel only if stats variance across channels > threshold
sasha: for regression protection, collect these metrics during calibration runs: token-level logprob MSE, generation-SIM (emb cosine), p95 latency, kv_cache_miss_rate
alex: i'm happy to run a controlled sweep. plan: 1k curated examples (stratified), runs: per-tensor, per-channel, per-channel+clip99.9, each with kv-warmup on/off and batcher windows [5ms,10ms,25ms]
alex: target to have results by EOD tomorrow if no objections
kevin: also add a small A/B in staging for 24h to check user-visible regressions (sample 1% traffic)
maria: +1. and add a quick kernel-selector rule: fallback to int8 for average seq_len<50 until we finish the tuning
ops-bot: scheduled job "fp8-calib-sweep-200543" created, will run with seeds 42/7/99 and post artifacts to /artifacts/calib/2005432190
jamal: neat. after we collect, let's update the kernel selector heuristics and add a KV cache warmup shim that can be toggled per-customer
sasha: last ask: capture a small sample of model activations for the 1k set so quantization debug can run offline (store gzipped tensors)
alex: ok will include activation dumps. thanks all.
kevin: cc @infra for possible allocator tuning if we see cudaMalloc stalls
alex: filing issue with results + PR template once sweep finishes
